remarks.name: Zara Zhang
remarks.role: Builder. Dangerously skips permissions. Harvard’17. GitHub: https://t.co/KCuEajezlL YouTube: https://t.co/8xzbGWtf6w
remarks.text:
When managers ask me how to train their nontechnical team on AI, my advice is always the same: run an install party

Everyone brings a laptop & you install the agents right there on their machines & get them to complete a meaningful task on the spot. Skip the abstract talk. Once it's installed, people start talking to the agent and learning from each other

The setup is 80% the barrier
remarks.translation: 当经理们问我如何对非技术团队进行AI培训时，我的建议始终如一：举办一场安装派对。每个人都带上笔记本电脑，当场在他们的设备上安装智能体，并让他们立即完成一项有意义的任务。跳过抽象的理论讲解。一旦安装完成，人们就会开始与智能体对话，并互相学习。安装环节占了80%的障碍。
remarks.observation: 这条言论可作为 Agent 产品形态、协作方式或能力边界的观察入口；只代表公开观点，不作为公司事实主证据。

remarks.name: Amjad Masad
remarks.role: ceo replit. civilizationist
remarks.text:
Sandboxes are hard.

With all the “AI escaping  sandbox” it’s easy to think “wow AI so scary,” but most AI companies, and recent “sandbox providers” are making very basic mistakes.

At Replit we’ve been running sandboxes since 2016 and targeted by every hacker and state actor under the sun. So we learned a thing or two. 

Main advice: Assume zero-days exist — because they do — and think in layers of protection in a zero-trust framework.

More here: https://t.co/3XGY0a1p3P
remarks.translation: 沙盒很难。面对各种“AI逃出沙盒”的说法，很容易让人想“哇，AI好可怕”，但大多数AI公司，以及最近的“沙盒提供商”，都在犯非常基本的错误。在Replit，我们从2016年起就一直在运行沙盒，并且被各种黑客和国家行为者盯上。所以我们学到了一些东西。主要建议：假设零日漏洞存在——因为它们确实存在——并在零信任框架中分层思考防护。更多内容：https://t.co/3XGY0a1p3P

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
The takeaway from this incident should not be that AI is scary. It should be that getting security right is incredibly important in the era of agents. 

Given the right tools and task, agents will do whatever it takes to get the job done, assuming enough compute. Thus, a misconfigured system - or something you thought was locked down but wasn’t - will become a risk vector. 

The core implications are less about the trust and safety of AI itself, but instead the work it’s going to take from enterprises to make sure they harden their environments. Lots of real work ahead for most organizations on this front.
remarks.translation: 这一事件的关键启示，不应是人工智能有多可怕，而在于智能体时代下，安全保障的极端重要性。只要配备合适的工具与任务，智能体便会不惜一切代价完成任务——前提是算力充足。因此，配置不当的系统，或是你以为已严密设防实则存在漏洞的环节，都将成为风险敞口。其核心影响与其说是关乎人工智能自身的信任与安全，不如说是企业需要付出大量努力来加固自身环境。在这方面，大多数组织前方还有大量实际工作要做。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
The cost of AI - normalized for the type of task - coming down is one of the most important factors in being able to drive further AI diffusion in the economy.

The general trend we should expect is that frontier AI models will continue to become more capable, and will look very expensive because the tasks that they can take on are more advanced. 

Then, shortly after, AI models will get more efficient or competition will drive more aggressive pricing dynamics, thus reducing the cost per task for anything other than the peak of the frontier.

This cycle will continue over and over again, which ultimately leads to tasks becoming cheaper on a like for like basis. And by doing so you will get even more AI adoption because now AI is more affordable for a wider variety of use-cases.
remarks.translation: 人工智能成本的下降——按任务类型标准化后——是推动人工智能在经济中进一步普及的最重要因素之一。我们应预期的大趋势是，前沿人工智能模型将继续变得更强大，并且由于它们能承担的任务更为先进，其成本会显得非常高昂。随后不久，人工智能模型将变得更高效，或者竞争将推动更激进的定价动态，从而降低除前沿巅峰之外所有任务的单位成本。这一循环将不断重复，最终导致同类任务在同等基础上变得更便宜。而这样一来，人工智能的采用率将进一步提升，因为现在人工智能对更广泛的应用场景来说变得更加经济实惠。

podcasts.name: Unsupervised Learning (Redpoint)
podcasts.title: 第90集：人工智能先驱尤尔根·施密德胡伯谈当今AI现状
podcasts.originalTitle: Ep 90: AI Pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber on the State of AI Today
podcasts.excerpt: 尤尔根·施密德胡伯博士，这位享誉全球的科学家与人工智能研究者，被公认为该领域的先驱之一。他通过其实验室的工作，孕育了当今Transformer架构、长短期记忆网络（LSTM）以及递归自我改进等关键理念。他认为，真正的通用人工智能（AGI）仍受限于物理硬件瓶颈；随着开源技术紧追封闭实验室的步伐，当前对AI数据中心的投资热潮即将迎来修正；而通往通用智能的路径，在于人工好奇心与自主生成的实验，而非依赖互联网数据。在结尾部分，他重新审视了主流AI安全论点，并描绘了一幅宏大愿景：自我复制的机器人社会终将殖民整个太阳系。 (0:00) 引言 (1:24) 超人类AI还有多远？ (2:27) ChatGPT为何未令他惊讶 (3:21) 递归自我改进之路 (9:01) AI会迎来爆发式飞跃吗…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Dr. Jürgen Schmidhuber, a renowned scientist and AI researcher widely regarded as one of the pioneers in the field, originated key ideas behind today's transformers, LSTMs, and recursive self-improvement through his lab's work. He argues that true AGI remains bottlenecked by physical hardware, that today's AI data center investments are headed for a correction as open-source keeps pace with closed labs, and that the path to general intelligence runs through artificial curiosity and self-generated experimentation rather than internet data. He closes by reconsidering mainstream AI safety arguments and offers a sweeping vision of self-replicating robot societies eventually colonizing the solar system. (0:00) Intro (1:24) How Close Is Superhuman AI? (2:27) Why ChatGPT Didn't Surprise Him (3:21) The Path to Recursive Self-Improvement (9:01) Will AI Takeoff…

podcasts.name: Unsupervised Learning (Redpoint)
podcasts.title: 第91期：顶级AI分析师解读当今AI炒作周期
podcasts.originalTitle: Ep 91: Top AI Analyst Unpacks Today's AI Hype Cycle
podcasts.excerpt: 科技界最受瞩目的分析师之一本尼迪克特·埃文斯做客雅各布·埃夫隆的节目。对话围绕本尼迪克特的核心论点展开：将人工智能的规模与过往平台变革（互联网、移动端、个人电脑）相提并论，在分析层面毫无意义；更具建设性的做法是研究那些技术实际的经济演进路径，从而推断人工智能的价值将沉淀在何处。他认为，这次真正的不同在于我们不清楚人工智能的物理或科学边界，而过往变革中这些边界至少是可预知的——正是这种不确定性，既助长了通用人工智能的狂热，也催生了末日论调，却未能解决任何实质问题。本尼迪克特剖析了为何能力仍呈锯齿状分布，导致使用场景同样参差不齐；为何编程凭借可规模化验证的特性，成为首个真正的企业级应用场景；以及为何绝大多数消费级和企业级用例，仍有待创业者们去开疆拓土……
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Benedict Evans, one of tech's most widely-read analysts, joins Jacob Effron. The conversation centers on Benedict's core thesis that comparing AI's scale to past platform shifts (the internet, mobile, PCs) is analytically useless, and that the more productive move is studying how those previous technologies actually evolved economically to reason about where AI's value will accrue. He argues the one genuine difference this time is that we don't know AI's physical or scientific limits, unlike past shifts where the boundaries were at least knowable, and that this uncertainty is what fuels both AGI hype and doomerism without resolving anything. Benedict unpacks why capabilities remain jagged, meaning usage is jagged too, why coding became the first real enterprise use case thanks to scalable verification, and why most consumer and enterprise use cases still have to be invented by entrepreneurs rat…
